statement: Holds the semantic version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) of this standard that the parser targeted when it ingested the event.
For an event parsed by a parser that ships in a package, the vendor name here must be the one used in the package scope (for example example_vendor for example_vendor/example_product).
Holds the version of ECS the parser follows.
Maps to the ECS event.kind field and is assigned in LogScale as an array.
Names, roughly, the product or service the event comes from. Reuse an existing event.module value whenever one fits.

CPS lists these tags for a compliant parser: #Vendor, #Cps.version, #observer.type, #ecs.version, #event.module, #event.dataset, #event.kind, #event.outcome. Two of them are conditional: #event.dataset and #event.outcome have their own rules.
notes: CPS 1.2 requires observer.type but does not define its accepted values. This record supplies the tag-presence requirement; presence alone does not establish value conformance.

statement: The parser leaves this field out when it would add nothing beyond what event.module already says.
condition: Created only when it would contain information beyond what is present in event.module. Absence is therefore not a violation.

statement: Maps to ECS event.outcome and is set only when the event can logically carry an outcome.
condition: Assigned only when an event can logically contain an outcome. Absence is therefore not a violation.

statement: Fields that do not exist in ECS get the literal prefix Vendor. in their names. ECS fields therefore stay in the root namespace, and every vendor-specific field can be found under Vendor.
notes: This is the rule behind prefix auto-naming: a Vendor.-prefixed field that no parser declares individually is the standard working as designed, not parser drift. A field in the root namespace that exists in no ECS release is the case this rule fails.

statement: Any field that does not come straight from ECS must start a capital letter at the point where its path diverges from the schema. A wholly custom field, such as Parser.version (like ecs.version but in a custom namespace), capitalizes its first segment. A custom field added to an existing ECS namespace, such as observer.Fictional_field, capitalizes only the new segment.

Leave Vendor. field names and values exactly as they appear in the source log so they correlate directly. The one exception: replace spaces in field names with underscores, so Vendor.User Name becomes Vendor.User_Name.

When assigning event.kind := "alert", also set event.severity, event.category[] and event.type[]; this matches the Common Information Model mappings that detection logic relies on. If those fields cannot be set, use event.kind := "event" instead.
condition: Applies only to events where event.kind is alert.
notes: Alert requirements depend on event.kind values; declared field names alone cannot establish conformance. CPS 1.2 references the Common Information Model for this rule.

statement: event.severity must map into 1-100. Scores 80-100 are critical, 60-79 high, 40-59 medium, 20-39 low and 1-19 informational; detection logic reads severity on this scale. The default is 50 when the raw event gives none.
notes: This rule constrains a value, so conformance requires observed values rather than declared field names alone.
